findings.summary: Self-caught during implementation: the L-20260814-01 registration was appended under a heading not named 'Registered', so parse_ledger silently skipped the row while `ledger.py check` printed CLEAN — a green over an unparsed entry (the §12 scope class: the check answered the question its selector asked, not the one the author heard).
findings.disposition: Heading renamed to 'Registered 2026-08-14 — …' in the same session; the row now parses (59 registered, verified through parse_ledger directly). Recorded as the taxonomy's first dogfood: a deterministic miss — no vacuity guard ties an appended block to the parser's section grammar.

findings.summary: Arch F1/F2: the A12 fix introduced a 9th root resolver that read only CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR — ignoring TDD_PLAYBOOK_PROJECT_ROOT, the adapter contract tdd_lock.py and _common.runtime_host declare for the Codex host this file is vendored to — and kept the old four-hop derivation as a live, untested fallback byte-identical to the defect A12 removed.

Arch F3: EXIT_VACUOUS gained a try/except literal fallback justified by a partial vendored copy the installer cannot produce (bin/ ships only as a whole tree) — an unreachable, untestable second home for a constant the repo's own plan says must never be re-typed.
findings.disposition: Hard-imported from dataflow_sweeps (the readable_surface pattern); the vendored-layout test now copies the real sibling set so the test tree matches the only layout the installer can produce.

findings.summary: Arch F4: the new calibration cycle block is the fifth copy-pasted isfile→run→print-or-unmeasured pointer block in run_calibration.py, diverging from its neighbours (prints stderr; resolves via REPO not HERE).
findings.rationale: The four prior blocks predate this plan; extracting a shared helper is a calibration-file refactor that belongs in its own reviewed change, not a drive-by here (§6 reverse check). The two divergences are deliberate, not drift: stderr carries the vacuous-refusal statement (the only pointer whose tool distinguishes empty-scan from clean), and REPO because review_ledger.py is the only pointed-at tool living outside calibration/. Revisit when a sixth block wants a home.

findings.summary: Arch F5: the six brief blocks pinned the class vocabulary to its owner but left TAXONOMY_SHIP_DATE as seven unpinned prose copies — slipping the future-dated constant by a day would leave six briefs stating a false refusal date under a green suite.

Arch F6: the roster pin anchored on the cardinality word ('four blocking guards') without validating it — five guards behind prose still saying 'four' passed — and phantom detection covered only README's full-name dialect, not CLAUDE.md's short-name slash-run.

Arch F7: the D-D test inlined a fourth hooks.json command traversal after the plan twice said to reuse host_parity's — literal reuse was impossible (the owner hardcoded the Claude path and returned basenames), which was the case for generalizing the owner, not forking it.
findings.disposition: host_parity.registered_scripts(hooks_json_path) is now the one parser (matches both hosts' root variables, returns plugin-relative paths); _guard_names and the D-D test both consume it.

findings.summary: Arch F8: _log_usage duplicates readable_surface's 12-line bootstrap-and-degradation wrapper around the single-owner write path (_common.log_yield_event).
findings.rationale: The write path already has one owner; what is duplicated is the sys.path bootstrap needed to REACH that owner, which cannot itself be shared without being bootstrapped first — a _common.log_usage helper would still leave the bootstrap and the except-degradation in every CLI, saving roughly two lines. The plan authorized the copy (A9). Revisit if a third CLI copy appears — three is where this becomes the pattern the repo's doctrine unifies.

findings.summary: Arch F9: catalog_row was gated on shape (^H\d+$), not membership — H99 validated and recurrence printed it as though it named a real HACK_CATALOG map row, while no machine reader of that table existed.

Tripwire note: the A8 review-recurrence cycle block runs only in opt-in real calibration runs (not --dry-run) and no test pins the block's presence in run_calibration.py — its removal would be silent until the next real cycle.
Tripwire note claimed the Phase-4 tdd-lock ceremony was not journaled (.claude/tdd-lock-journal.jsonl last entry 2026-08-07).
findings.rationale: Refuted by direct read: the lock and the feature-end unlock are journaled in .git/tdd-playbook/events.jsonl — the lock's ONE versioned authority under Git's common dir (the TEST-LOCK design) — with the red-commit sha 8641b70 and the full reason. The auditor checked a .claude/ path the tool does not use.

findings.summary: The Stop-hook auto-checkpoint swept the user's deliberately-untracked .codex/config.toml into tracked history (8ea214b) — the SKILL 11 class: auto-checkpoints must exclude state another actor holds; a sweep that adds files the session's own commits deliberately excluded is silent scope creep.
findings.disposition: Untracked again at 1d4f892 after verifying the file holds no secrets (a benign local exitcode_guard opt-in, so the 8ea214b blob staying in unpushed-then-pushed history is acceptable); .codex/ added to .git/info/exclude — local-only, so no repo policy is set for a directory the owner left untracked.
